_what: Now Playing: one screenprinted bill pasted on the poster column on the pavement, beside the Pebble Board. Every room on this street with something in it to press and play, what is on there, and what that room puts on first. Read by tools/make-now-playing.py. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-25.
_first: NOTHING ABOUT WHAT IS ON FIRST IS WRITTEN IN THIS FILE. The tool reads each room's PUBLISHED PAGE and takes the first thing on it you can press -- a press-to-play button, a channel on a set, a headset -- after the point named in `after`, with the title and the runtime exactly as that room prints them. A poster whose top line was typed would be a claim about another room living in this one's copy, which is the shape CLAUDE.md warns about most often, and it would go on naming last month's opener the day the room changed it. So the only things here are OUR words about each room, and the marker in the room's page where its running order starts.
_what_is_ours: The `what` line on each venue is ours, written for this poster, and nothing is lifted from the room it describes. It still repeats that room's claims about itself, so each one carries `holds`: words on the room's published page that carry what the line says. The tool reads the page and refuses when they have gone -- make-community.py's rule, for make-community.py's reason.
_order: There is no order in this file that the poster uses. The bill runs in the sitemap's walking order, read out of make-sitemap.py, which is the order you would reach the rooms in walking down the street and out past either end. No headliner: every venue's name is set the same size, and the tool refuses the vocabulary of a top billing. A gig poster is exactly the shape of thing that puts one act in big letters, and on this street that would be one room ranked above the others by a poster that belongs to all of them.
_where: Where each room is -- on the street, behind another room, in the campgrounds, down the road out of town -- is not written here either. It is read off data/map.json's rooms-behind-rooms and off which page links to the room: the campgrounds' board, the Outskirts' signs, the front page's doors.
_bill: EVERY ROOM WITH SOMETHING TO PRESS IS ON THE BILL, and the tool finds them by looking rather than by being told. A page carrying a press-to-play facade, a set with a running order in it, or a headset is a venue; one that is not on this bill and not in `left_off` with a reason stops the build. So a room cannot open with a stage in it and be missing from the poster, which is make-sitemap.py's refusal of an unlisted page, arriving at a listing.
_nothing_plays: NOTHING ON THE POSTER PLAYS. It is paper. It says where to go and what is on first when you get there, and every one of those waits for you to press it in its own room. The tool refuses a facade, a frame or an audio element anywhere on the page, because a poster that could play a song is a second jukebox with nobody's room around it.

venues.what: The dancefloor. A jukebox of songs our own pages already credit, and decks of whole playlists off our own channel to put on and leave running.
holds: Every song we have ever hung on a page lives in here, in one jukebox

venues.what: A rhinestone chapel of Chappell Roan videos, one to a niche, and the whole playlist put on at the east end.
Freaks to the front. A punk club with every playlist we keep on the stage and a rack of records along the back wall, and nothing in there strobes.
A burrow under the hill for burnouts, with a wireless playing ocean waves and a television showing seated tai chi.
A viewing room under a canopy, with the nature live cams from our Watering Hole Hangs page. None of it ends, so nothing in there says how long it runs.
Elvis Presley’s den at Graceland, and the songs cut on its green shag in 1976, in the order they were recorded and with the writers named on every one.
A cold library with a parlour screen that plays one song a great many ways, most of them on a cello.
A shaft you fall down on purpose, with the recordings off our own glossary entry on rabbit holing.
A comedy club down a ramp. Disabled comics on their own terms, off our Disabled Comedy playlist, in the order we put them in.
A picture house where every screening is a relaxed screening: house lights up, captions on, and films about autism, ADHD and neurodiversity, most of them made by the people they are about.
holds: Every screening is a relaxed screening

venues.what: A plant-based kitchen where everything in the bowl touches, and the stereo plays songs about food.
A control room with the red light on, and sessions played in a studio rather than at a gig: Austin City Limits, KEXP and KCRW so far, every one saying how long it runs.
holds: While the red light is on

venues.what: Daily news, usually bad: a parlour after closing with a tub of the news in the cabinet for every morning of the week, from the independent news, the late-night shows and the YouTubers, and then it is gone.
holds: A week, and then it is gone

venues.what: Show-and-tell under glass, right beside this column: the songs and videos our people brought each other at a gathering, one edition at a time.

Helen’s candlelit yurt at the edge of the woods: Sophie Broadgate’s short film In Motion in the Stim Tin in her Regulation Nook, Vi Hart’s Moon Spoon through the window by the pebbling pot, and under the phonograph a songbook of her yarn, which plays next door in the Music Room.

Helen’s Reading Room, through the door by the bookshelf in her yurt: a gramophone among the bookcases with her library playlist on it, to switch on and off, and a shelf of records off it to take out one at a time.

Helen’s music room, through the door by the phonograph in her yurt, and the one place her playlists play: whole on the phonograph, or a record at a time off their shelves, with nothing else to scroll past.

Helen’s picture palace, through the cinema door in her yurt: every film she keeps as an old-fashioned reel on a rail, whole channels and playlists among them, each going up on the screen when it is pressed.
holds: Every film, as reels on the rails

venues.what: Down and into the rhizome under Helen’s yurt: films of living light, from fungi glowing on a wood’s floor to the deep sea, each up on the hollow’s screen when it is pressed.
Through the round door in Helen’s yurt: a film for families to make a lava lamp that glows under a black light, up on the pod’s screen when it is pressed.
Jess’s tree house at pitch 05, up in an autumn grove, where one song plays on repeat.
David’s cabin at the summit over the campgrounds, where his own playlist goes on the big screen and one switch runs the room.
A meadow left alone, with a real fire burning in the pit in the clearing and Robin Wall Kimmerer in her own voice round it.

A cabin on wheels under solar panels, with a speaker in the cave's curtain playing one playlist, and one television at the campfire with a channel listing of documentaries to have on while you get on with something else.
A woodland tea room at pitch 04, lit by its own wood, with other people's woodland tea rooms in the looking-glass by the window.
A wildlife sanctuary seen on the night round by warmth, with a month of films from people who look after animals and the wild on the screen in the keepers' hut.
holds: The screen in the keepers’ hut
people who look after animals and the wild

venues.what: A cannabis farm in glowing hoop houses, with films about growing among companion plants, hemp to rope and cloth, and rosin on the screen in the potting shed.
holds: The screen in the potting shed
hemp stalks into rope and cloth

venues.what: A mixed farm between two lights, with films about growing, grazing and the Three Sisters, and the last month of Farming While Beige, on the screen in the barn.
A garden sown by throwing seed into the wind, with films about chaos gardens, meadows from seed and plants that sow themselves on the screen in the seed shed.
holds: The screen in the seed shed

venues.what: A solar farm at noon with peppers in the panels' shade, and films about crops, sheep and bees under solar panels on the screen in the battery shed.
holds: The screen in the battery shed
crops, sheep and bees under solar panels

venues.what: A drive-in screen standing in black water where it is always Halloween: our Halloween playlist on the screen and The Cramps on posts in the water. Nothing out there flickers.
An open-air stage under rock faces glowing with lichen, and whole concerts on it, every one saying how long it runs.
A silent disco on an old airstrip: one crate of our dance-punk playlist on three headsets, and the volume in your own hand.
holds: Three channels, and they are one crate started in three places

venues.what: An all-night diner with Josephmooon on the jukebox, and Up All Night, a Stimpunk’s song about Autistic insomnia, on the counter.
A mushroom farm with a restaurant at the end of it, and Derek Sarno cooking mushrooms: his whole Mushroom Masterclass on one press, and his most recent videos in a rack.
A brewery and cellar in the rock, every pour alcohol-free first, and somebody else's cellars on long videos to leave running.
An old hangar by the airstrip, with festival films on the big screen and the street's one strobe, off until you switch it on and say yes.
holds: Nothing is fetched from YouTube until you press something
the one place on the street where you will see a strobe

venues.what: A haunted house built of plywood in a warehouse at the end of the road, and Enigma’s soundtrack for it, Hallowscenes, made with Suno, which plays only when you press a piece.
holds: the one thing in the house that makes a sound

venues.what: A lighthouse keeper's watch room behind the Events door at Cavendish Coworking, with a screen on the wall and Schitt's Creek on the rack to watch together.
holds: Each video on the rack says how long it runs

venues.what: A pan of water in the desert at noon, behind a door at Cavendish Coworking, with the Jungle Room's desert, otter and jelly cams to leave on.
holds: each one runs until you close it

venues.what: A fire in a clearing at night, behind a door at Cavendish Coworking, with a ring of logs and the fire pit at Swaying Sweetgrass's real campfires to leave burning.
holds: each with how long it runs

venues.what: The quiet room inside the ice, behind a door at Cavendish Coworking, with real caves to leave running while nobody says anything.
holds: each with how long it runs

venues.what: A desk under a window with a notebook lying open on it: Ryan's piece on bullet, junk and interstitial journaling, and the videos it points at, on the laptop beside it.
A glasshouse at night under red and blue grow lamps, about learning, making and knowledge gardening with AI, with the latest month from AI channels on the bench screen.
A community kitchen with its windows steamed up, where nobody is turned away, with the last month from cooking channels on the teaching screen.
A cat café with a window at every height and every cat from the shelter, with films from other cat cafés on the telly by the hatch.
A pub under the street with no screens and a player piano, and a shelf of old rolls, some of them played onto the paper by the people who wrote the music.
A dog park in a dog's colours, every dog from the shelter out for a run, and television made for dogs on the dog telly on the porch.
Five food trucks round a covered porch, nothing with a price on it, and films about tacos, bánh mì and ramen on the screen on the side of the Cooler.
A community green space just after the rain, and films about cities making room for green on the screen under the porch roof.
holds: The screen under the porch roof
cities and towns making room for green

venues.what: A junk playground, and adventure playgrounds from Wales to Berkeley on the old telly on the Pile.
holds: The old telly on the Pile

venues.what: Isha Snow's tiny home by the Columbia River, where the creativity corner holds her own podcast episodes and her talk show.
holds: Everything I've made, or am still making.

venues.what: Kristina Brooke's salon at desert dusk, where every record on her shelf pairs a few of her words with one song and one strain.
holds: Each record holds a grouping of words, music, and bud.

venues.what: The street’s room for asking, and Vivian Ly’s talk at Autscape 2020 on Autistic mutual aid, where the four things its channel is for come from.
A cab at night in the middle of a convoy, lit only by marker lamps, for CB radios, CB slang and the long haul, with Dale Watson’s Truckin’ Sessions and Convoy on the rack.
holds: Not a line of any of these songs is on this page.

left_off.about.html: The About page's film says what the street is, for anybody who does not get it yet. It is an explanation and not something on in a room, so the poster, which says what each room puts on first, has no line for it.
